clauses.reason: The order approves the Code of Fair Competition for the Construction Industry under Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act; its operative words are "do order that the said Code of Fair Competition be and it is hereby approved". Under section 3 of Title I an approved code supplied the standards of fair competition (3(b)), equity enforcement by the district courts (3(c)) and criminal liability for violations (3(f)), so the command had no operative effect apart from section 3. Section 2 of Senate Joint Resolution 113, approved on the date stated in the resolution as "Approved, June 14, 1935.", provides that all the provisions of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes "are hereby repealed"; the resolution states no other effective date for section 2. The approval therefore ceased to operate on June 14, 1935. A. L. A. Schechter Poultry Corp. v. United States, decided May 27, 1935, is recorded as a validity characterization (the section 3 code-making delegation was held unconstitutional; under the doctrine then prevailing an approval made under it was void from issuance), not as an end date, because no held record shows that the government cancelled or suspended this code on that date. June 16, 1935, the original two-year expiry of Title I, is not an end: section 1 of the resolution replaced that expiry with "on April 1, 1936", and nothing in the resolution defers section 2.

research_rationale:
Executive order approving the Code of Fair Competition for the Construction Industry under section 3 of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act. Applying the reviewed shared analysis: the code-dependent command has no own-terms end, no held record shows an earlier cancellation or suspension, and Senate Joint Resolution 113 section 2 (June 14, 1935) repealed the code approval and enforcement provisions, so the approval ended on June 14, 1935. Schechter (May 27, 1935) is a validity characterization, not an end date. The text is an American Presidency Project transcription held as a provisional working text under the 2026-10-21 owner ruling; no certification is claimed.

savings.reason: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the Code of Fair Competition for the Construction Industry before June 14, 1935, and any fine, injunction or conviction already completed, are accrued effects that the repeal did not undo; the section 5 antitrust exemption for action already taken under an approved and effective code is likewise an accrued effect. The proviso to section 2 of the resolution names agreements and action thereunder and states no time limit, and the held text does not settle whether it narrowed that exemption for past action under codes. No held source continues the approval after June 14, 1935, and no held source shows a prosecution under this code continued after that date; nothing here continues the approval itself.

United States judgment: the section 3 code-making delegation was held unconstitutional and the code provisions in question invalid; recorded as the validity characterization that applies to every section 3 approval, not as an end of this order.
